subject: chemistry
title: Group 1: the alkali metals
key_idea: The Group 1 elements are the **alkali metals**. Each has one electron in its outer shell, which it loses easily to form a 1+ ion. They react with water to make hydrogen and an alkaline solution, and they get more reactive going down the group.

blocks.text: The alkali metals are lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium and francium. This section covers their physical properties.

items.meaning: The elements in Group 1 of the periodic table.
A solution containing hydroxide ions (OH⁻), with a pH above 7.

items: They have one electron in the outer shell. This is why they are in the same group and have similar chemical properties.
They are soft metals, soft enough to cut with a knife, with relatively low melting points.
The melting points decrease going down the group.
They have a low density. Lithium, sodium and potassium float on water. Rubidium is denser than water and sinks.
They are stored under oil so that they do not react with air (oxygen) or water.
They form ions with a 1+ charge, such as Na⁺, by losing the outer electron.
Group 1 metals have one outer electron and form 1+ ions.
They are soft with low melting points and low density.
Their properties depend on the single electron in the outer shell.

blocks.text: The alkali metals react with oxygen, chlorine and water. In each reaction the metal atoms lose their outer electron.

items: The metal floats, moves around on the surface and gets smaller until it disappears.
Bubbles (effervescence) of hydrogen gas are given off.
The solution formed is an alkali. Universal indicator turns blue, purple or violet.
Hydrogen gives a squeaky pop with a lighted splint.

diagram.alt: Pick an alkali metal to see what happens when a small piece is added to water.
diagram.prompt: Pick an alkali metal to add to water

options.label: Lithium
results: Floats, moves slowly and bubbles slowly
Lithium hydroxide solution, which is alkaline, and hydrogen gas

options.label: Sodium
results: Floats, melts into a ball, moves quickly and bubbles quickly
Sodium hydroxide solution, which is alkaline, and hydrogen gas

options.label: Potassium
results: Floats, melts into a ball, moves very quickly, bubbles very quickly and burns with a lilac flame
Potassium hydroxide solution, which is alkaline, and hydrogen gas

options.label: Rubidium
results: Sinks, melts into a ball and explodes with a flame
Rubidium hydroxide solution, which is alkaline, and hydrogen gas

items: Before: sodium is a silver solid and chlorine is a green gas.
During: hot sodium burns with a yellow or orange flame and the green colour fades.
After: a white solid, sodium chloride, is left.
Alkali metal + water → metal hydroxide + hydrogen. The solution is alkaline.
Alkali metal + oxygen → metal oxide. Alkali metal + chlorine → metal chloride.
Use a small piece of metal and a large trough of water to react safely.

blocks.text: Reactivity increases going down Group 1. The reason is in the electrons.

items.text: Atoms lower down the group have more shells, so the outer electron is further from the nucleus.
There is more shielding, so the attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron is less.
The outer electron is lost more easily, so the metal is more reactive.

items: Lithium has the electronic structure 2,1 and potassium has 2,8,8,1.
Potassium has more shells than lithium, so it is more reactive.
Use the pattern to predict rubidium and caesium: they react more violently than potassium.
Reactivity increases down Group 1.
The outer electron is further from the nucleus, less attracted, and lost more easily.
Use the trend to predict the reactions of rubidium and caesium.

checks.q: Give two observations when a small piece of potassium is added to water.
checks.a: Any two from: it floats, melts, moves around, becomes smaller, effervescence (fizzing), a lilac flame.

checks.q: Write a balanced equation for the reaction of lithium with water.
Explain why rubidium is more reactive than potassium.
checks.a: The outer electron in rubidium is further from the nucleus, so there is less attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron. It is lost more easily.

worked_example.question: Explain why the reactivity of elements changes going down Group 1.
answer_points: Reactivity increases going down the group.
The outer electron (shell) is further from the nucleus, or there are more shells.
So there is less attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron.
So the atom loses an electron more easily.
worked_example.tip: State the trend first, then give the chain of reasons. More shielding is also accepted.

worked_example.question:
Lithium, potassium and rubidium are alkali metals.

The electronic configuration of lithium is 2.1
The electronic configuration of potassium is 2.8.8.1
Lithium is less reactive than potassium.

Explain, in terms of their electronic configurations, why lithium is less reactive than potassium.
answer_points: The outer electron in lithium is closer to the nucleus.
So there is more attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron.
Therefore the electron is harder to lose.
worked_example.tip: Fewer shells, a smaller atomic radius or less shielding all score the first point. The reverse argument for potassium is also credited.

worked_example.question:
The Group 1 elements all react with Group 7 elements to form ionic compounds.

The Group 1 elements become more reactive down the group.

Explain why.
answer_points: Down the group the outer shell electron is further from the nucleus.
There is less attraction between the nucleus and the outer shell electron, or more shielding.
The outer electron is lost more easily.
worked_example.tip: Each point is marked independently. Refer to the outer shell electron at least once to get all 3 marks.

worked_example.question:
Group 1 elements have lower melting points and lower boiling points than transition elements.
Describe two other physical properties of Group 1 elements that are different from transition elements.

items: Three trends going down from lithium, sodium and potassium: the melting point decreases, the density generally increases and the reactivity increases.
Predict the properties of another Group 1 element from these trends. Caesium is softer than potassium, has a lower melting point and reacts even more violently.

worked_example.question: Explain, in terms of electron configuration, why sodium is more reactive than lithium.
answer_points: The outer shell is further from the nucleus in sodium (sodium has more shells)
There is less attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron in sodium
So the outer electron is more easily lost
worked_example.tip: Lithium is 2,1 and sodium is 2,8,1. Talk about the outer electron, not electrons in general.
